title: L,S,A,Q and N
notes:
Dimensions of Common Physical Quantities

Understanding dimensions requires knowing how each physical quantity is defined. For any derived quantity, write its defining formula first, then substitute the dimensions of each constituent quantity. Speed v = distance/time → [M⁰L¹T⁻¹]. Velocity has same dimensions as speed: [M⁰L¹T⁻¹]. Acceleration a = \Delta v/\Delta t → [M⁰L¹T⁻²]. Momentum p = mv → [M¹L¹T⁻¹]. Force F = ma → [M¹L¹T⁻²] (Newton). Work/Energy W = Fd → [M¹L²T⁻²] (Joule). Power P = W/t → [M¹L²T⁻³] (Watt). Density \rho = m/V → [M¹L⁻³T⁰]. Pressure P = F/A → [M¹L⁻¹T⁻²] (Pascal).

Gravitational and Mechanical Quantities

Gravitational constant G: From F = GMm/r², [G] = [F][r²]/[M]² = [MLT⁻²][L²]/[M²] = [M⁻¹L³T⁻²]. Surface tension T = F/l → [M¹L⁰T⁻²]. Viscosity \eta = F/(A \cdot dv/dx) → [F]/[L²][LT⁻¹][L⁻¹] = [MLT⁻²]/[LT⁻¹] = [M¹L⁻¹T⁻¹]. Moment of inertia I = mr² → [M¹L²T⁰]. Angular velocity \omega = \theta/t → [M⁰L⁰T⁻¹]. Angular momentum L = mvr → [M¹L²T⁻¹]. Torque \tau = r \times F → [M¹L²T⁻²]. Modulus of elasticity Y = stress/strain → [ML⁻¹T⁻²]/[1] = [M¹L⁻¹T⁻²]. Mass density of energy u = Energy/Volume → [ML²T⁻²]/[L³] = [M¹L⁻¹T⁻²] (same as pressure).

Thermal and Optical Quantities

Specific heat capacity s = Q/(m\Delta T) → [ML²T⁻²]/[M][K] = [M⁰L²T⁻²K⁻¹]. Thermal conductivity k = Qx/(A \cdot \Delta T \cdot t) → [ML²T⁻²][L]/[L²][K][T] = [M¹L¹T⁻³K⁻¹]. Entropy S = Q/T → [ML²T⁻²]/[K] = [M¹L²T⁻²K⁻¹]. Refractive index n = c/v → dimensionless [M⁰L⁰T⁰]. Power of a lens P = 1/f → [L⁻¹] (Diopter). Focal length f → [L]. Wave number \bar{\nu} = 1/\lambda → [L⁻¹]. Luminous flux \Phi → [J] (candela). Illuminance E = \Phi/A → [JM⁻²].

Electrical Quantities

Electric charge q = It → [T¹I¹]. Electric potential V = W/q → [ML²T⁻³I⁻¹] (Volt). Electric field E = F/q → [MLT⁻²]/[T I] = [MLT⁻³I⁻¹]. Resistance R = V/I → [ML²T⁻³I⁻²] (Ohm). Conductance G = 1/R → [M⁻¹L⁻²T³I²] (Siemens). Capacitance C = q/V → [T²I²M⁻¹L⁻²] (Farad). Permittivity \epsilon_0: From Coulomb's law, [\epsilon_0] = [Q²]/[F][L²] = [T²I²]/[MLT⁻²][L²] = [M⁻¹L⁻³T⁴I²]. Permeability \mu_0: From force between wires, [\mu_0] = [MLT⁻²][L]/[I²][L²] = [MLT⁻²I⁻²]. Magnetic flux \Phi_B = B \cdot A → [ML²T⁻²I⁻¹] (Weber). Magnetic field B = F/(Il) → [MT⁻²I⁻¹] (Tesla).

Atomic and Quantum Quantities

Planck's constant h = E/\nu → [ML²T⁻¹] (same as angular momentum). Boltzmann's constant k_B = R/N_A → [ML²T⁻²K⁻¹] (same as specific heat per molecule). Activity of radioactive substance A = \lambda N → [T⁻¹] (Becquerel). Mean free path \lambda = 1/(\sqrt{2}\pi d²n) → [L]. Diffusion coefficient D → [L²T⁻¹]. Stefan-Boltzmann constant \sigma = P/(A T⁴) → [M¹T⁻³K⁻⁴]. Wien's displacement constant b = \lambda_max T → [L][K] = [M⁰L¹T⁰K¹].

Dimensionless Quantities

Several important quantities are dimensionless (have [M⁰L⁰T⁰] or equivalent): Angle \theta = arc/radius (ratio of two lengths). Solid angle \Omega = A/r² (ratio of two areas). Strain \epsilon = \Delta L/L (ratio of two lengths). Refractive index n = c/v (ratio of two velocities). Specific gravity = \rho_substance/\rho_water (ratio of two densities). Coefficient of friction \mu = F_friction/F_normal (ratio of two forces). Poisson's ratio = lateral strain/longitudinal strain. Dielectric constant K = C_with_dielectric/C_without. Dissipation factor tan \delta = 1/(\omega RC). These are pure numbers but may carry names of units (radian, degree).

Principle of Homogeneity

The principle of homogeneity of dimensions states: 「An equation is dimensionally correct only if the dimensions of all terms on both sides are identical.」 This is applied in three ways: (1) Checking equations — verify every term has same dimensions. Example: s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at² → [L] = [LT⁻¹][T] + [LT⁻²][T²] = [L] + [L] ✓. (2) Deriving formulas — assume P depends on l, g, m and find exponents. (3) Unit conversion — n₂ = n₁ × (u₁/u₂) using dimensional powers. Important limitation: Dimensional analysis cannot determine dimensionless numerical constants (like ½, \pi, 2\pi) or derive formulas involving trigonometric/exponential functions.

Checking Dimensional Correctness — Worked Examples

Example 1: Check s = u + \frac{1}{2}a(2n-1) (distance in nth second). [s] = [L]. [u] = [LT⁻¹]. [a(2n-1)]: Here n is the nth second (number), so (2n-1) is dimensionless. [a] = [LT⁻²], but this gives [LT⁻²] ≠ [LT⁻¹]. However, in this formula n is actually TIME (n seconds), so [a \cdot n] = [LT⁻²][T] = [LT⁻¹]. The equation is correct when n represents time. Example 2: Check F = ma → [MLT⁻²] = [M][LT⁻²] ✓. Example 3: Check V = IR → [ML²T⁻³I⁻¹] = [I][ML²T⁻³I⁻²] = [ML²T⁻³I⁻¹] ✓.

Dimensional Analysis for Deriving Relations

When a physical quantity depends on several other quantities, dimensional analysis can find the relationship. Method: (1) Assume the form Q = k \cdot A^a \cdot B^b \cdot C^c where k is dimensionless. (2) Write dimensions of both sides. (3) Equate powers of M, L, T on both sides. (4) Solve simultaneous equations. Example: Find the period T of a simple pendulum depending on length l, mass m, and gravity g. Assume T = k \cdot l^a \cdot m^b \cdot g^c. [T] = [L]^a [M]^b [LT⁻²]^c. Equating: M: b = 0; L: a + c = 0; T: -2c = 1 → c = -½, a = ½. So T = k\sqrt{l/g}. Experiment gives k = 2\pi. Note: Mass m does NOT affect the period!
confusion: Same dimensions do NOT mean the same physical quantity — Pressure [ML⁻¹T⁻²] and stress [ML⁻¹T⁻²] share dimensions but represent different concepts (force/area vs. internal restoring force/area); torque [ML²T⁻²] and work [ML²T⁻²] share dimensions but torque is a vector, work is a scalar.

The principle of homogeneity checks DIMENSIONS, not numerical correctness — s = ut + at² has correct dimensions on both sides but is physically wrong (missing factor ½); only dimensional consistency, not correctness, can be verified.

Dimensionless quantities may still have units — Angle is dimensionless [M⁰L⁰T⁰] but measured in radians or degrees; these are named units, not dimensional units. Similarly, decibel (dB) for sound intensity level is dimensionless.

In dimensional analysis, you can find at most THREE unknown exponents — With three fundamental dimensions (M, L, T), you get three equations. If your assumed formula has more than three unknown powers, the system is indeterminate and dimensional analysis alone fails.

Power is NOT the same as pressure dimensionally in all contexts — While [Power] = [ML²T⁻³] and [Pressure] = [ML⁻¹T⁻²] are different, power per unit area (intensity) = [ML²T⁻³]/[L²] = [MT⁻³], which is different from pressure. Always check the FULL dimensional formula.

Exact numbers have infinite significant figures and zero dimensions — The '2' in T = 2\pi\sqrt{l/g} is exact (count), so it has no dimensions and doesn't affect the dimensional balance; similarly, the '4' in area of circle = \pi r² doesn't add dimensions.

Trigonometric ratios are dimensionless — sin\theta, cos\theta, tan\theta all have [M⁰L⁰T⁰] because they are ratios of lengths (opposite/hypotenuse, etc.). When using dimensional analysis, trig functions don't contribute dimensions.

Frequency and angular frequency have the SAME dimensions but different meanings — Frequency \nu has [T⁻¹]; angular frequency \omega = 2\pi\nu also has [T⁻¹]. They differ by the dimensionless factor 2\pi, which dimensional analysis cannot resolve.
practice: Show that the dimensional formula of surface tension is [ML⁰T⁻²]. [Solution: Surface tension T = Force/Length = [MLT⁻²]/[L] = [ML⁰T⁻²]. SI unit: N/m or kg/s².]

Using dimensional analysis, derive the relation for the time period T of a simple pendulum in terms of its length l and acceleration due to gravity g. [Solution: Assume T = kl^a g^b. [T] = [L]^a [LT⁻²]^b = [L^{a+b}T^{-2b}]. Equating: a+b=0, -2b=1 → b=-½, a=½. T = k\sqrt{l/g}. Since k is dimensionless, experiment gives k=2\pi. So T = 2\pi\sqrt{l/g}.]

The velocity v of sound in a gas depends on pressure P and density \rho. Find the relation using dimensional analysis. [Solution: Assume v = kP^a \rho^b. [LT⁻¹] = [ML⁻¹T⁻²]^a [ML⁻³]^b = [M^{a+b}L^{-a-3b}T^{-2a}]. Equating: M: a+b=0; L: -a-3b=1; T: -2a=-1 → a=½, b=-½. So v = k\sqrt{P/\rho}. (For ideal gas, P/\rho = \gamma RT/M, giving v = \sqrt{\gamma RT/M}.)]

Check the dimensional correctness of Kepler's third law: T² = \frac{4\pi^2}{GM} r³. [Solution: LHS [T²] = [T²]. RHS: [G] = [M⁻¹L³T⁻²], [M] = [M], [r³] = [L³]. RHS = [M⁻¹L³T⁻²]⁻¹[M]⁻¹[L³]² = [M¹L⁻³T²][M⁻¹][L⁶] = [L⁶T²][L⁻³]... Let me recalculate: [4\pi²/GM] × [r³] = [1]/([M⁻¹L³T⁻²][M]) × [L³] = [M L⁻³ T²] × [L³] = [T²]. LHS = [T²] ✓. Dimensionally correct.]
Find the dimensions of universal gas constant R from PV = nRT. [Solution: [R] = [PV]/[nT] = [ML⁻¹T⁻²][L³]/[N][K] = [ML²T⁻²K⁻¹N⁻¹]. SI unit: J/(mol·K) = kg·m²/(s²·mol·K).]

If the units of force, energy, and velocity are 10 N, 100 J, and 5 m/s respectively, find the units of length, mass, and time in this system. [Solution: [F] = [MLT⁻²] = 10, [E] = [ML²T⁻²] = 100, [v] = [LT⁻¹] = 5. From v: L = 5T. From E/F: L = 100/10 = 10 m. So T = L/5 = 2 s. From F: M = F \cdot T²/L = 10 \times 4/10 = 4 kg. Answer: Length = 10 m, Mass = 4 kg, Time = 2 s.]

Show that the dimensions of Planck's constant h are the same as angular momentum. [Solution: From E = h\nu, [h] = [E]/[\nu] = [ML²T⁻²]/[T⁻¹] = [ML²T⁻¹]. Angular momentum L = mvr = [M][LT⁻¹][L] = [ML²T⁻¹]. They are identical! This is why h has units of J·s = kg·m²/s, same as angular momentum.]

The drag force on a sphere moving through a viscous fluid is given by Stokes' law: F = 6\pi \eta r v. Check its dimensional correctness. [Solution: [F] = [MLT⁻²]. [6\pi] is dimensionless. [\eta] = [ML⁻¹T⁻¹], [r] = [L], [v] = [LT⁻¹]. RHS = [ML⁻¹T⁻¹][L][LT⁻¹] = [MLT⁻²]. LHS = RHS ✓. Dimensionally correct.]

Using dimensional analysis, find how the frequency f of a vibrating string depends on its length l, tension F, and mass per unit length \mu. [Solution: Assume f = kl^a F^b \mu^c. [T⁻¹] = [L]^a [MLT⁻²]^b [ML⁻¹]ᶜ = [M^{b+c}L^{a+b-c}T^{-2b}]. Equating: M: b+c=0; L: a+b-c=0; T: -2b=-1 → b=½, c=-½, a=-½. So f = k\sqrt{F/l\mu} = k\frac{1}{l}\sqrt{F/\mu}. (Experiment gives k = \frac{1}{2} for fundamental mode.)]

Express 1 Joule in a system where the fundamental units are 100 g, 10 cm, and 1 s. [Solution: [W] = [ML²T⁻²]. New value = 1 × (1 kg/100 g)¹ × (1 m/10 cm)² × (1 s/1 s)⁻² = 10⁻¹ × 10² × 1 = 10. So 1 Joule = 10 new units of energy in this system.]
universalFacts: Dimensional analysis was systematized by Fourier in 1822 but the underlying idea goes back to Newton — Newton recognized that meaningful physical equations must be independent of the units chosen. Einstein later used dimensional arguments to predict the photon momentum p = E/c.

NEB exam tip: For deriving formulas using dimensional analysis, always mention the 'limitation' — You CANNOT find the dimensionless constant k (like 2\pi, ½, 4\pi). These must be determined experimentally. Mentioning this shows complete understanding and earns full marks.

The dimensions of physical constants reveal deep connections — Planck's constant [ML²T⁻¹] connecting energy and frequency; gravitational constant [M⁻¹L³T⁻²] connecting force and mass-distance; Boltzmann's constant [ML²T⁻²K⁻¹] connecting thermal energy and temperature. Each bridges different domains of physics.

Dimensionless groups govern similarity in engineering — Reynolds number Re = \rho vD/\eta determines whether flow is laminar or turbulent. In wind tunnel testing, models are designed to match Re of the full-scale object. These dimensionless numbers are PURE results of dimensional analysis.

When converting units, only the dimensions matter, not the specific units — 1 N = 1 kg·m/s² = 10⁵ g·cm/s² = 10⁵ dyne. The conversion factor is determined entirely by the dimensional formula [MLT⁻²], independent of which particular units you choose.

The dimensional formula [ML²T⁻³I⁻²] appears for resistance, but also for inductive reactance and impedance — All have the same dimensions as resistance. This is why RL, RC, and RLC circuits can be analyzed with consistent dimensional bookkeeping.

In the SI system, the ampere is now defined via the elementary charge e — Since 2019, 1 ampere = 1 coulomb/second where the coulomb is defined by fixing e = 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. This makes electrical dimensions traceable to quantum physics, not macroscopic force measurements.
